takes.prompt: A single uninterrupted locked-off tripod wide shot, photoreal casino game show footage. Preserve EXACT framing, camera, studio, wheel centre and size, and the same adult female presenter in blue from the image throughout. The wheel is a physical vertical wheel, not floating. No zoom, pan, cuts, reframing, overlays or subtitles. Natural human anatomy, weight shift, breathing, eye focus and fingers. At 0-2 seconds she looks to camera and speaks clearly in a warm Indian female voice, with accurate lip sync: 'Bets are closed. Let's spin the wheel!' At 2-3 seconds she turns toward the wheel and reaches her LEFT hand to grasp the outer rim on the right side, at the two o'clock position. At 3-4 seconds she firmly PULLS the rim DOWN clockwise towards four o'clock, with visible hand-to-rim contact and physical effort, then releases. The wheel starts moving only as she pulls it and coasts clockwise. Her hand stays on the outer rim, not crossing the inner face. At 4-8 seconds she lowers her hand and watches the spinning wheel attentively with a natural excited smile; ticking of wheel pins gradually slows. At 8-10 seconds she turns smoothly to camera and returns to the exact starting stance. Only the wheel disk rotates; the rim frame, pedestal and pointer remain fixed. No cheering crowd, no music, only her clear voice and natural mechanical ticks. High-end broadcast cinematography, realistic skin and cloth, fluid human performance, not robotic.

No camera motion, cuts, subtitles or overlays. The wheel stays COMPLETELY STILL for the whole shot. Natural lifelike blinking, breathing, small head movements and weight shifts. She speaks to the camera in a warm confident Indian female voice with precise realistic lip sync: 'Welcome to Wheel two point zero! Choose your lucky number, and place your bets.' She speaks during the first five seconds, gently inviting with her right hand towards the game, while keeping her body beside the wheel. High quality natural broadcast footage, not an animated mannequin.
